headline: SK hynix expects the performance of AI computing infrastructure to grow about 20-fold by 2030 as demand for running AI models rises.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a company outlook with no method or figures behind the 20-fold claim.
importance_line: It shows where a leading memory maker sees demand heading, which points to continued need for memory in AI systems, but the 20-fold figure is a company projection and Yonhap does not say what "performance scale" measures.
summary: Yonhap reports that Ahn Hyun, head of development at South Korean memory-chip maker SK hynix, told the Semiconductor Exhibition (SEDEX) in Seoul on 14 Oct 2026 that the performance of AI infrastructure will grow roughly 20-fold by 2030, driven by demand for inference, the stage at which trained AI models answer users. He said memory is becoming central, because the growing "KV cache" (stored data that an AI model reuses) must be spread across several memory types, and that SK hynix is working on 3D stacked DRAM and High Bandwidth Flash while improving its current high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
